title: Frontend: Power of Two
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Power of Two. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution(n). Return whether a safe positive integer is an exact power of two. Invalid, fractional, zero, and negative values return false. Support powers beyond 32 bits.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
For a safe-integer Number, reject nonpositive or noninteger values and divide by two while the remainder is zero; accept exactly when the final value is one.
alternativeApproaches: Implement Number and BigInt variants with separate input contracts rather than mixing numeric types.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: 1; 0; negative value.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
